#1859. Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenham right-back conundrum in new Pedro Porro injury update

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted he has yet to decide whether to restore Pedro Porro to the starting lineup ahead of Tottenham’s trip to Leeds.

The Spaniard was named on the bench as Spurs made it three wins in a row with a 2-0 victory at home to Crystal Palace last weekend.

De Zerbi said after the game that the decision not to start the right-back, who recently returned to fitness after a month out with a hamstring injury, came from the player himself, who told his manager that he did not feel comfortable playing from the off.

Porro had initially injured his hamstring after insisting he was ready to start Spurs’ 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa in September before coming off injured after just 19 minutes.

De Zerbi was prepared to listen to his vice-captain ahead of the Palace game, even though he said post-match that he believed Porro was fit enough to start.

The Italian seemed confident that there were no issues with his full-back last weekend but he was reluctant to confirm whether he would be available to start at Elland Road.

“I have not decided yet about Pedro Porro, but it is not a tactical decision,” the head coach said.

“When Pedro Porro is fit, he plays because he is a top player, top guy, leader, clear leader, without problems.”

Porro has started just three of Spurs’ first nine league games this season, leaving Archie Gray to deputise in his absence.

The versatile Englishman has carved out an important role for himself in De Zerbi’s side and was promoted to the team’s five-man leadership group at the start of the season.

Gray leads the Premier League for underlapping runs and has made more sprints than any Spurs player this term, with De Zerbi describing him as a “very smart player”.

“Archie Gray is one of the best players in this moment, as a condition, as a confidence. He is playing very well,” De Zerbi continued.

Three years on, and Gray has developed into a jack of all trades, a leader on the pitch and someone De Zerbi believes can be instrumental to Spurs and England’s future.

“Gray is a leader, a young player, but is different leader. He is a leader on the pitch because he has personality even if he is very young.

“I think, like I said last season, he is the future of this club for the national team as well, and it is not important if it is not very clear his position on the pitch because for many players it is something more than less to be able to play in different positions on the pitch. #1858. Sunderland vs Chelsea - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 14:33, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:48

Needing nothing short of a minor miracle to replicate their 2025-26 feats against Chelsea, Sunderland host the Blues in Sunday's Premier League fixture at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats trail their visitors by 16 places and 11 points in the Premier League table at the time of writing and face Xabi Alonso's well-rested men after a sobering defeat in Europe too.

The meeting between two erstwhile Premier League midfield maestros last weekend saw Alonso pile more misery onto Michael Carrick, whose Manchester United side had the better of the opening 45 minutes at Stamford Bridge before an all-too familiar implosion.

Morgan Rogers waltzed his way past a disorganised Red Devils defence to propel the Blues into the lead, before Lisandro Martinez's senseless red card and Cole Palmer's penalty put paid to any hopes of a Mancunian fightback.

Snapping a two-game losing sequence in all competitions and earning their third win from their last four Premier League matches, Chelsea's triumph coupled with Liverpool losing to Arsenal saw the Blues consolidate fourth spot in the rankings, one clear of the Reds and three worse off than Brighton & Hove Albion.

The Blues' sorry defeat to Tottenham Hotspur raised questions about how Alonso's squad can cope in the absence of influential attacker Joao Pedro, but Chelsea answered those critics in gameweek nine to earn their first Premier League home win with a clean sheet since January.

Fifteen goals conceded still makes the visitors the worst defensive unit in the top 10, though, while they have shipped eight in five away games in all tournaments; seven of those came in their first three road matches, though, and they have since allowed just one in their last two on rival turf.

However, Alonso's side now square up to one of the four teams with a worse backline tally than them in the 2026-27 Premier League, and one without Chelsea's colossal firepower to make up for it.

The second season syndrome cliche is very much appropriate for Sunderland, whose measly five-point total places them bottom of the Premier League standings, although 17th-placed Man United are only two points better off.

The Black Cats have shown little signs of survival spirit in recent weeks, though, as last weekend's humbling 3-1 loss to newly-promoted Coventry City marked their fifth defeat from their last six Premier League games and extended their winless run in the division to seven.

Stadium of Light was also awash with boos on Thursday night, when Regis Le Bris's men went down 2-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League, ending their unbeaten start in the tournament and leading to renewed sack talk.

The Sunderland hierarchy are not minded to remove Le Bris from his post just yet, though, and the Frenchman's focus now turns to repeating last season's shock 2-1 home and away wins against Chelsea, but not since 2001 have the Black Cats bested the Blues in three straight games.

Chelsea boss Alonso confirmed a triple fitness boost in his pre-game press conference, revealing that Emiliano Martinez is in contention to return from his jaw operation, while Aaron Anselmino and Jordan Henderson have battled back from injury and illness respectively.

The latter's presence may be crucial this weekend, as Moises Caicedo missed training earlier this week due to discomfort, and there are no guarantees that he will be fit to face the Black Cats.

Jorrel Hato (unknown), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) Reece James (knee), Jamie Gittens (ankle) and Joao Pedro (quad) are confirmed absentees for Chelsea, whose playmaking star Cole Palmer will have a particular point to prove this weekend after being omitted from Thomas Tuchel's England squad yet again.

As for a jaded Sunderland side, Omar Alderete serves a one-game ban following his sending-off at Coventry, but Nordi Mukiele should exit concussion protocols in time to deputise for his fellow defender.

Daniel Ballard (hamstring), Habib Diarra (muscle) and Romaine Mundle (knee) will not return before the international break, though, while teenage striker Juan Riquelme Angulo is uncertain due to a contact injury.

Le Bris ripped up his second-string side in midweek, making no fewer than four half-time changes, so expect the likes of Trai Hume, Reinildo, Enzo Le Fee, Noah Sadiki and Brian Brobbey to return here.

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, O'Nien, Reinildo; Xhaka, Sadiki; Rigg, Le Fee, Angulo; Brobbey

Penders; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Palestra; Henderson, Lavia; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Neto

Fatigue should not play a significant role for Sunderland on Sunday given the alterations Le Bris made in midweek, but backing the Black Cats to get anything out of any Premier League game at present is a tough ask.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

#1856. Brest vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 06 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:33

On a mission to record back-to-back wins, Brest welcome title-chasing Lyon to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Sunday afternoon for a Ligue 1 contest.

Les Pirates picked up a comfortable success at Lorient last time out, whereas Les Gones have been busy on continental duty, sharing the spoils at Real Sociedad.

After a mediocre 12th-placed finish in Ligue 1 last season, Brest are aiming to qualify for European competition this time around, with their recent form suggesting that a continental charge could be successful.

Les Pirates have lost just one of their past four top-flight matches after picking up a 2-0 away triumph at Lorient on Monday night, when Ludovic Ajorque and Noah Edjouma found the net in the second half.

Aiming to record consecutive top-flight victories for the first time since early March, Brest are currently occupying 10th position in the Ligue 1 standings, eight points behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain.

Rather surprisingly, only four of Les Pirates' 12 league points have been collected at Stade Francis-Le Ble so far this campaign, with Julien Lachuer's men winning only one of their opening four home contests.

That sole success was impressive and emphatic in equal measure, though, as leading marksman Ajorque provided a goal and an assist in a 5-1 battering of relegation-threatened Angers on October 10.

Following back-to-back wins over Anderlecht and Conference League champions Crystal Palace to commence their Europa League campaign, Lyon have earned just one point from clashes with Hoffenheim (0-3) and Real Sociedad (1-1).

In fact, Les Gones have won just one of their past four matches (D1 L2) across all competitions, with their most recent away league outing ending in a 2-0 victory for PSG at Parc des Princes.

However, Jorge Maciel's troops were able to strengthen their faint title hopes last Sunday afternoon, when goals either side of the half-time break from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso were enough to beat Angers.

That success extended their unbeaten home league run to five matches (W4 D1) and moved Lyon up to third position in the Ligue 1 table, just three points behind Luis Enrique's European champions.

Les Gones are unbeaten across their past three encounters (W2 D1) with Brest; however, Les Pirates are unbeaten in the past three meetings (W2 D1) between the sides at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

Brest are expected to be without the services of Brendan Chardonnet, who is sidelined for up to two weeks because of a calf problem.

Les Pirates' options at centre-back are further reduced by the absence of 20-year-old Raphael Le Guen.

A high-profile loanee from Juventus, Lois Openda is currently in the Lyon treatment room because of a leg injury.

With the Belgian set to return after the international break, Nuamah is an important source of goals this weekend for Les Gones.

Wanted by Championship side Wrexham in the summer, Pavel Sulc is out until January with a knee injury.

Selvik; Lala, Tousart, Lloris, Locko; Chotard, Magnetti; Balde, Doumbia, Mboup; Ajorque

Greif; Athekame, Bacher, Niakhate, Abner; Bidstrup, Tessmann, Tolisso; Duranville, Nakamura, Nuamah

#1855. New pope, rise of Luke Littler and what that has happened since Spurs last won four games in a row

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

It has been 1,108 days since Tottenham last won four Premier League games in a row - a run they could end this weekend when they face Leeds at Elland Road.

Not since the opening months of Ange Postecoglou’s reign have Spurs won more than three times in succession - a feat they quickly achieved twice either side of a north London derby draw under the Australian between August and October 2023 - and a lot has happened in the intervening three years.

That season, fast-starting Tottenham won eight of their first 10 fixtures and went five points clear at the summit despite the high-profile summer loss of Harry Kane to Bayern Munich, eventually finishing in fifth place.

Here, Standard Sport looks at some of the biggest stories to have happened since Spurs last won four on the bounce.

Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected as the 267th Pope of the Catholic Church in May 2025, taking the name Pope Leo XIV.

While Pope Leo is said to be a Real Madrid fan, he was gifted a Sunderland shirt with the name "Pope Leo, 14" emblazoned on the back ahead of the club’s Europa League campaign.

Pope Leo was gifted the shirt after Sunderland’s chaplain, Father Marc Lyden-Smith, gave one to Pope Francis ahead of the Black Cats’ victory over Newcastle in 2013.

Donald Trump was re-elected as President of the United States in November 2024, defeating Democratic candidate and former vice-president Kamala Harris.

It came four years after Mr Trump had lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden, ending his initial spell in the White House after victory over Hillary Clinton in 2016.

The Labour Party came back into power after 14 years as Sir Keir Starmer was elected as UK Prime Minister in July 2024.

Despite a landslide victory, Starmer resigned in July 2026 and was replaced by Andy Burnham.

The UK has now had five Prime Ministers in the last five years.

Daniel Levy stepped down as executive chairman of Tottenham in September 2025, bringing to an end his 25-year reign at the club.

Following Levy’s departure, non-executive chairman Peter Charrington declared “a new era of leadership for the club” before Spurs went on to endure their worst season in Premier League history as they only narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship on the final day.

Tottenham would have been relegated had they not mustered up a nervy 1-0 win at home to Everton on the final day of last season.

Man City XI vs Nottm Forest: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Tottenham XI vs Leeds: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Where to watch Leeds vs Tottenham: TV channel and live stream

12 months after lifting the Europa League, their first major trophy for 17 years, Spurs would remarkably become mired in a relegation battle with rivals West Ham, staying up by the skin of their teeth thanks to a goal from loanee Joao Palhinha.

Spurs’ decision to get rid of Postecoglou just 16 days after he guided them to Europa League success over Manchester United in Bilbao was always going to prove controversial.

No one, though, could have foreseen the disaster that would unfurl over the next season as Tottenham went through three managerial changes in 10 months.

Thomas Frank was brought in as Postecoglou’s successor, but was eventually sacked in February 2026 with the club hovering over the relegation zone.

His replacement, Igor Tudor, lasted just 44 days before the club hit the panic button again to bring in Roberto De Zerbi to steer them to safety.

In the space of three years, West Ham went from Conference League winners to being relegated to the Championship.

A series of poor recruitment decisions, managerial changes and ownership uncertainty ensured the Hammers failed to build on their first piece of major silverware in 43 years before eventually dropping back to the second tier after 14 seasons.

Darts sensation Luke Littler announced himself on the biggest stage at just 16 years old as he made a historic run to the World Championship final on his debut at Alexandra Palace in January 2024.

Since then, Littler has become a back-to-back world champion and underlined his place as the best player on the planet while still a teenager.

Another sporting prodigy, Kimi Antonelli has risen from obscurity to the top of his sport in the last three years.

At just 20 years and 68 days old, Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula One world champion in history on Sunday after clinching the 2026 title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

A record-breaking campaign has also seen Antonelli become the youngest winner of the Monaco Grand Prix, the youngest driver to achieve a Grand Slam, and the first Italian in more than 60 years to be crowned world champion.

Sir Andy Murray and Rafael Nadal retired within a few months of each other to leave Novak Djokovic as the last man standing from the ‘Big Four’ era of 21st century tennis.

Two-time Wimbledon winner Murray retired in August 2024 and was swiftly followed by 22-time Grand Slam champion Nadal in October. It followed Roger Federer’s retirement in September 2022.

Boxing fans have long since grown weary of Tyson Fury’s retirement U-turns, so his fourth announcement last year that he was hanging up his gloves convinced few. Just a handful of months later, he made the decision to step back into the ring for a fifth, and surely, final time in April 2026.

The former world heavyweight champion beat Russian Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decision in his first fight back and is now gearing up for a hotly-anticipated bout with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff in December, having also defeated Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

#1853. Celtic boss Martin O'Neill and board given 'hard but fair' grilling by fans in Greenock

Published: 15:16 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EDT, 3 November 2026

Martin O’Neill and senior Celtic board members were subjected to ‘hard but fair’ questioning in a meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, the club have revealed.

The manager was joined by chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials for a two-and-a-half-hour question-and-answer session that revolved around recruitment, transfer policy, communications and the club’s ambitions and strategy.

Representatives from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs supporters clubs were among around 120 Celtic fans who attended ‘to seek information and voice concerns’.

Martin O'Neill and the Celtic board met supporters in Greenock

The meeting came just a day after Celtic’s 2-0 defeat at Falkirk left them with just three wins from their past 10 matches in all competitions.

O’Neill, whose own position has come under intense scrutiny recently, told the Hoops’ website: ‘I asked to attend the meeting because I want to meet supporters as much as I possibly can.

‘We have had a few difficult weeks in recent times and I understand our supporters’ frustrations, but my resolve and the commitment of the players is as strong as ever to continue to bring success and progress to the club.’

Wilson vowed that the club would take on board concerns raised by supporters.

‘We were grateful to the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for hosting this event in a way that allowed everyone to make their points, many of them critical, and to ask questions which we did our best to answer,’ the chairman said. ‘We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.’

#1851. Europa League preview: AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan are back in front of their own fans on Thursday night, hoping to correct their European course against Ferencvaros.

Milan are buoyed by the derby win over Inter at the weekend, and yet in continental competition they have struggled so far having lost two of three. So, the pressure remains on to bounce back and start climbing the Europa League table before it is too late.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his pre-match press conference, Ruben Amorim admitted that his side needed to find some consistency, especially after the win against Inter. Effectively, his message was that the win would mean little if it wasn’t followed with another three points.

Game date: Thursday, November 4 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Urs Schnyder (VAR: Fähndrich)

As mentioned above, Milan could hardly be going into this game feeling any better after they scored three first-half goals to down their city rivals for a fourth straight time. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored in a 3-1 win that was well engineered by Ruben Amorim.

The Rossoneri continue to demonstrate their potential domestically, even if they remain seven points off top, but in the Europa League things haven’t gone to plan. Losses to Benfica and Bournemouth – both without scoring – either side of the rout of RB Salzburg leave them on three points from three games.

That puts Milan in 24th place in the table on goals scored, which is the final play-off spot. So, a big improvement is needed in the final five games of the league phase in order for the tag of being among the pre-tournament favourites to be justified.

Mario Gila, Rabiot and Moreira all returned to the line-up against Inter, which provided a very noticeable boost. However, there are no new recoveries in view of the match against Ferencvaros, so the depth is still limited.

Fikayo Tomori is in the treatment room after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh, joining Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze who also remain out. The latter may yet require surgery on a hip issue.

The other major absentee is Mike Maignan, who saw red for shoving Tyler Adams in the face during the last Europa League game against Bournemouth and will be forced to serve a one-match ban, which is less than feared.

The latest from the various media reports suggests that Amorim will field quite a youthful side, as he has done in Europe so far. This means chances should be given to Lorenzo Torriani, Sankhoun Diawara, Ardon Jashari, Davide Bartesaghi, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and potentially more.

Expectations about rotation seem likely to be proven right, with the defence being almost completely changed. Without a back-up, Torriani is indeed given the nod.

Then, the backline is made of a largely rotated group. Filippo Terracciano will start at right-back, whilst Koni De Winter will partner Diawara in the middle of the back four. Bartesaghi returns at left-back.

In midfield, Hutchinson and Cisse will start on the flanks as expected, with Yunus Musah and Jashari given the nod in the middle of the park.

Despite suggestions that Camarda could start, it seems Goncalo Ramos will be given the starting role again.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Comotto, Modric, Moreira, Pulisic, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Maignan, Pavlovic, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

This will be the first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros, making it a historic encounter as a result.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match. Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencáros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026/2027.

➤ AC Milan will look to build on their derby success when they welcome an unbeaten Ferencváros side to the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday evening. Ruben Amorim’s team have enjoyed a promising domestic campaign but struggled to replicate that form in Europe, occupying 24th place in the league-phase standings with just three points from their opening three matches. Their Hungarian opponents, meanwhile, sit fourth with a perfect nine-point return and arrive in Italy chasing a fourth consecutive European victory.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter Milan at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing. They suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11. Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures. Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967/68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level. Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

Sankhoun Diawara has been superb so far when called upon, and he’ll replace the ever-present Strahinja Pavlovic here. A big performance would not only reassure the club of his ability (and potential), but it may offer a reason to change January plans.

It feels like a weekly occurrence now, but Goncalo Ramos needs a goal. If Francesco Camarda is not going to start here, the Portuguese needs to prove that there is reason to keep the youngster on the bench. For his sake, as much as the Italian’s.

For the visitors, Kristoffer Zachariassen is the main danger man. Contributing to 11 goals in 21 games so far this season, the 32-year-old will be essential to Ferencvaros getting anything on Thursday.

Then, Mariano Gomez will represent a difficult opponent for whoever leads the Rossoneri’s line. The Argentine defender has been excellent so far this season, and it’s entirely possible that he contributes to a frustrating night.

Despite their rotations, Milan must win here; if they don’t, they’ll wave their Europa League top eight wishes goodbye. There’s enough quality in the starting XI to provide three points, so that will be the expectation.

#1850. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal want Aston Villa star; new Man Utd manager twist; Chelsea, Liverpool latest

The January transfer window is approaching, with Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all exploring moves to strengthen their squads for the second half of the season. Arsenal are reportedly targeting Antonio Nusa, while also keeping tabs on Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus midfielder Kenan Yildiz. Mikel Arteta is also said to be interested in Alex Baena and Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly rejected the opportunity to become Manchester United manager, with Sunday's trip to Aston Villa potentially crucial for under-pressure boss Michael Carrick. Tottenham are also understood to retain matching rights for Harry Kane, despite the England captain signing a record-breaking new Bayern Munich contract that reportedly makes him Europe's highest-paid player by basic salary.

Chelsea are confident of securing a deal for Alex Scott when the window opens, while Liverpool are monitoring Mexico youngster Gilberto Mora and Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara. Trent Alexander-Arnold, meanwhile, continues to be linked with a surprise return to Anfield after leaving for Real Madrid. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Arsenal have been told they lead the race for Antonio Nusa ahead of a £50million January transfer battle for the RB Leipzig winger.

Former Norway midfielder Kristoffer Lokberg believes Nusa is now ready to make another step in his career and says Arsenal are the strongest option.

Speaking on NRK's Bakrommet podcast, via Sport Witness, he said: “He is one of the world’s most exciting left-wingers. We have been waiting for his potential to come to full bloom, but now it is exploding.

“Big clubs can no longer sit on the fence, they must act quickly before he disappears, or they will be left regretting it.”

Lokberg continued: “The completely obvious option in the Premier League is Arsenal.

“The player fits their playing style, and the club has a real need. They basically only have Tzolis and a slightly half-hearted Eberechi Eze as options on the left wing. I think Arsenal sit around every day, weighing whether to pull the trigger.”

Manchester United are considering several candidates as they assess their options for the managerial position, but there are reservations about a number of the names linked with the job.

Eddie Howe has for some time been considered the frontrunner for the role, should Michael Carrick get sacked, but The Independent report that the former Newcastle manager is less highly regarded by Man Utd than other reports have suggested.

Julian Nagelsmann is the other highly prominent name, though his reputation has suffered following his time at Bayern Munich and with the Germany national team. Man Utd’s interest is said to be driven by the club’s recruitment chief, Christoph Vivell, but others are less convinced amid concerns over Nagelsmann's relationship with players during his time with the national team.

A new wildcard name in the frame is Stuttgart manager Sebastian Hoeness, who his appointment would be considered another big gamble after the likes of Ruben Amorim failed spectacularly. The Independent also mention Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler, but it is feared he could find it difficult to replicate his success on the south coast should he move to Old Trafford.

Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are keeping tabs on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki following his impressive start at Villa Park.

The 24-year-old Japan international has attracted interest from several European giants after arriving from Parma for £30m in the summer.

According to TEAMtalk, Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Tottenham are also monitoring Suzuki’s progress.

PSG previously considered signing him, while Real Madrid view him as a potential long-term successor to Thibaut Courtois.

However, Villa are under no pressure to sell, having tied the goalkeeper down to a five-year contract and viewing him as central to Unai Emery’s plans.

Christos Tzolis has hailed the role played by Cristhian Mosquera to help him acclimatise to life at Arsenal.

The Greek international signed for the Gunners back in the summer to replace Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli on the left flank.

He has hit the ground running since his £34million move from Club Brugge,as he returned to the English top flight for the first time since 2024, when he ended a fruitless three-year spell at Norwich City.

Now, after some impressive performances across all competitions, the winger has revealed the Arsenal star that has helped to settle him in London.

Manchester United have been bolstered in their pursuit of a left-back.

The Red Devils have been hamstrung in that position this term, with natural options Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu both struck down with injuries that have kept them out for long spells.

As such, it has forced under-fire manager Michael Carrick to experiment with makeshift solutions in the interim, with right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui both depuitising there, while central defender Ayden Heaven has also been shifted out wide to cover with limited success.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down an approach over the Manchester United manager’s job, as more details emerge over the future of Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been subject to severe scrutiny for several weeks now following a miserable eight-game winless run across all competitions that was the club’s worst since the 1988/89 season.

Such a dire sequence was only snapped on Tuesday night as Man Utd staged an incredible turnaround following an abysmal first half to beat depleted Roma 3-2 at home in the Champions League, though it remains to be seen how much respite that offered their beleaguered head coach.

Sky Sports report that there remains support for Carrick within the United hierarchy, who have been said to be split on a potential replacement amid strong links to the likes of former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Real Madrid look to have won the race for Manchester United sensation JJ Gabriel.

The teenage star shocked Old Trafford chiefs back in September by stating his desire to leave the club immediately, just days before he was expected to make his senior debut aged just 15.

All of the rest of the heavyweight clubs across Europe were inevitably interested in signing one of the brightest youth talents in England, but Real Madrid and Barcelona quickly emerged as the front runners.

Madrid were said to be leading the race, with Fabrizio Romano now reporting that Gabriel has chosen the Bernabeu and that his camp have informed all parties of his decision.

The move is expected to be sealed soon, with Man Utd likely only due minimal training compensation.

Tottenham retain matching rights on Harry Kane despite his new Bayern Munich contract, reports claim.

The England captain yesterday put pen to paper on a lucrative contract extension in Bavaria until 2029 that is said to make him the highest-paid player in Europe in terms of base salary.

That bumper new deal does not impact Tottenham’s first-option right to match any future bids for Kane, per The Telegraph.

That agreement was reached during his initial exit from Spurs in 2023 and is said to lie outside of his contract, so has been unaffected.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly told Manchester United that he is not interested in taking over as manager at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick’s future as Man Utd boss remains hugely uncertain ahead of Sunday’s crunch home Premier League clash with Aston Villa, which is likely to prove pivotal.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann had previously been considered as the leading candidates for the role if United - who will not consider an interim solution this time - were to sack Carrick, though FootMercato in France reported on Thursday that the club had also approached former long-time Les Bleus head coach Deschamps.

However, he is said to have told them that he currently has no interest in the job in another blow to the beleaguered Red Devils.

Arsenal are tracking Antonio Nusa ahead of the January transfer window, reports claim.

The Gunners are known to be keen on attacking reinforcements when the market reopens for business in the New Year and have reportedly had their eyes on Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz.

However, The Sun say that Arsenal are also keeping close tabs on former Club Brugge star Nusa, who continues to impress for both RB Leipzig and Norway.

Could a lucrative triple deal yet be in the offing at the Emirates Stadium after a somewhat disappointing summer?

#1849. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

OFF: Shaw, Dorgu, Lacey, MaguireON: Armer, Amass, Zirkzee, Williams

Big save from Heaton to deny Atletico at the near post after Yoro was beaten by a lovely pass from Lemar.

The energy and intensity of the first half has largely disappeared in this half. Neither keeper has been worked.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.

J. Fletcher coming for United in place of Amad.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#1848. JJ Gabriel has set himself a huge target at Real Madrid

Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he moves closer to joining Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old gave an interview to Spanish newspaper Marca while training individually in Madrid, having not returned to United since requesting to leave the club in September.

Gabriel was presented with a front page of the newspaper featuring himself and responded: "Can I keep it?"

The forward was also asked why he preferred Real Madrid to Barcelona, with the teenager making his choice clear by replying: "Obviously, Madrid."

He then outlined his biggest ambition in football, saying: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or."

Gabriel is understood to have reached a verbal agreement with Real Madrid, who are hoping to complete the move in January. The Spanish club are planning for him to develop with their reserve side, Castilla, before potentially progressing into the first team.

The teenager has already spent time training in Barcelona before moving to the Spanish capital, where his representative Ali Barat is handling negotiations and helping arrange accommodation for Gabriel and his family.

His Irish passport is expected to make a move to Spain possible under FIFA regulations allowing certain players aged 16 to 18 to transfer within the European Union. However, Gabriel remains registered with United, meaning he cannot yet represent another club.

United are disappointed to lose one of their highly-rated academy prospects and had attempted to persuade him to stay by offering a new contract and a pathway towards senior football.

The club could receive training compensation if the transfer is completed, with reports suggesting the figure could be around £350,000.

Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut and was named Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season last term.

#1847. Elche vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 14:48, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:51

Real Betis will aim to make it successive wins in Spain's top flight when they continue their campaign against Elche at Estadio Martinez Valero on Sunday afternoon.

The visitors posted a 2-1 victory over Malaga in their last league match, while Elche will enter the contest off the back of a 1-0 home defeat to Valencia.

Elche boast a record of two wins, four draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 10 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

The Green-Striped Ones were beaten 1-0 by Valencia in their last match, but that proved to be their first loss in five games in all competitions.

Martin Anselmi's side have actually won two of their last three matches, including a 3-1 victory over Pinatar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Elche have struggled in their recent meetings with Real Betis, losing four of the last five fixtures between the two sides, but the corresponding game last season finished 1-1.

The Green-Striped Ones have not managed to overcome Real Betis since April 2022, while their last home success over the Seville outfit came back in November 2009.

Real Betis lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 24 wins to Elche's 16, while 17 of their 57 games have finished all square.

Manuel Pellegrini's side were in Champions League action during the week, suffering a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in the league stage of the competition.

The Seville outfit were 2-1 winners over Malaga last time out, with that success making their record seven wins, two draws and two defeats from their 11 league matches this season, which has left them fourth in the table on 23 points.

Real Betis are only four points off third-placed Real Madrid and are, as expected, firmly in the Champions League picture at this stage of the La Liga campaign.

El Glorioso have a record of two wins, two draws and one defeat from their five away league matches this season, scoring six times and conceding seven.

Elche will be without the services of Marc Aguado and Thomas Lemar for this weekend's match through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong form.

Yago Santiago and Gonzalo Villar had both been doubts for this contest, but the pair are available for selection, while Pedro Bigas should also again be in the squad.

Lemar's position in the starting side is likely to be taken by Facundo Buonanotte, while there will be a spot through the middle for Fer Nino, who has netted six times in La Liga this season.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez remains on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back in the fold for the Seville outfit until the end of November.

Facundo Bernal is still suspended, but Junior Firpo and Alvaro Fidalgo are both expected to be back in the squad after recent absences.

Troy Parrott has not scored for Real Betis since the start of September, but the 24-year-old is expected to continue through the middle for Pellegrini's team.

Dituro; Sangare, Chust, Redondo, Revivo; Villar, Morcillo; Cepeda, Buonanotte, Valera; Nino

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Roca, Fornals; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

Elche have been in solid form of late, and this is not a straightforward match for Real Betis, but we are backing the Seville outfit to secure a valuable three points on Sunday.

#1846. Arsenal told why Antonio Nusa will join them in £50m January transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been told they lead the race for Antonio Nusa ahead of a £50million January transfer battle for the RB Leipzig winger.

The Gunners are expected to make attempts to improve their attack in the upcoming mid-season transfer window, in light of their struggles up front, and Nusa has been heavily linked in recent days.

The 21-year-old Norway international has attracted interest after an impressive start to the season which has seen him score six goals and provide seven assists in 13 Bundesliga appearances.

Nusa is less experienced then other reported Arsenal targets, such as Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus wonderkid Kenan Yildiz, but could been more attainable in January.

Former Norway midfielder Kristoffer Lokberg believes Nusa is now ready to make another step in his career and says Arsenal are the strongest option.

Speaking on NRK's Bakrommet podcast, via Sport Witness, he said: “He is one of the world’s most exciting left-wingers. We have been waiting for his potential to come to full bloom, but now it is exploding.

“Big clubs can no longer sit on the fence, they must act quickly before he disappears, or they will be left regretting it.”

Leipzig are reportedly demanding at least £50m for Nusa, though Lokberg believes a figure closer to £40m could force the club’s hand.

Lokberg continued: “The completely obvious option in the Premier League is Arsenal.

“The player fits their playing style, and the club has a real need. They basically only have Tzolis and a slightly half-hearted Eberechi Eze as options on the left wing. I think Arsenal sit around every day, weighing whether to pull the trigger.”

#1845. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

🔁 Últim canvi al Girona:➡️ Stuani⬅️ Pyshchur

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

🔁 Més canvis al Girona:➡️ Gibert, Holmes, Izan, Misehouy i Jastin⬅️ Arnau, Fran Beltrán, Francés, Bryan i Minsu pic.twitter.com/fb7aVKloFx

Kabia gets to the byline and intelligently pulls a cross back to Gabriel Jesus, who curls a first-time strike narrowly wide of the far post as Arsenal search for a fifth goal.

Meslier showcases his magnificent reflexes, making a world class save to deny the recently-introduced Ruiz from close-range after he latched onto Martinez’s dangerous delivery.

Both sides make numerous changes to their line-ups to manage minutes and give the younger players some game time.

A flurry of substitutions...↩️ Arrizabalaga, White, Tzolis, Nwaneri, Dowman, Vieira, Mosquera, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly🔛 Meslier, Nelson, Kabia, Ibrahim, Copley, Clarke, O'Neill, Harriman-Annous, Ogunnaike🔴 1-4 🔵 (61) pic.twitter.com/GDXL0JRzkT

🔁 Canvis al Girona:➡️ Krapyvtsov, Antal, Badia, Iván Martín, Abel i Pyshchur⬅️ Gazzaniga, David López, Van de Beek, Lass, Àlex Moreno i Vanat pic.twitter.com/3T6Pb9d9fG

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

🎯 El gol d'Arnau pic.twitter.com/Op6oX3LBzK

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

A dominant first-half display in Girona 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ZprG2xLYyj

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

We're making a triple substitution...↩️ Havertz, Hincapie, Gyokeres🔛 Vieira, Salmon, Jesus🔴 0-2 🔵 (32) pic.twitter.com/NtpnUsfAY6

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡©️ White with the armband✨ Nwaneri floating in the middle🆕 Tzolis from the startAnother pre-season test awaits, LIVE on The Arsenal 📺 Presented by @deel 🤝

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

The FA Cup continues apace this weekend with the draw for the second round.

The FA Cup first round ties began on Friday night with 2021 winners Leicester seeing off Oxford City. Elsewhere, 2013 winners Wigan are aiming to avoid an early exit at the hands of Boreham Wood.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds and Stafford Rangers - the lowest-ranked teams remaining in the competition - face off against Burton Albion and Grimsby Town respectively, raising the prospect of a major giant-killing.

Here’s everything you need to know about the FA Cup draw for the second round...

The draw for the FA Cup second round will take place on Monday, November 9, 2026, before the clash between non-league clubs Plymouth Parkway and Berkhamsted.

Television coverage of the game starts at 6:30pm GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The ball numbers are to be confirmed closer to the second round draw.

#1842. Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Sunderland: Emi Martinez, Moises Caicedo decisions made

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 14:58

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is in contention to make his return from injury in Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

The Argentina international has made an excellent recovery from his sickening head collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, which left him needing jaw surgery.

However, Martinez is now back in the picture to put the pressure back on Mike Penders, who made up for a dodgy debut against Tottenham Hotspur with a hard-fought clean sheet against Manchester United last weekend.

As momentum is on Penders's side, Xabi Alonso may feel that he can err on the side of caution with Martinez, and the former has our vote to hold his spot in between the sticks.

Penders should be shielded by an unchanged backline in Josh Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Marco Palestra, as Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jorrel Hato are all still unavailable.

Alonso may be forced into a midfield alteration, though, as Moises Caicedo is suffering from discomfort, so Jordan Henderson - fully fit again after an illness - could join forces with Romeo Lavia.

Left out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad once more, all eyes will be on Cole Palmer, as the 24-year-old lines up with Estevao Willian, Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers in another Joao Pedro-less attack.
